messages:
alex: Heads up, seeing nvme multipath heartbeat failures in eu-west1; devices are flapping during GPU attach and ~75 GPU attach requests are queued. Attach-controller shows devices disappearing.

maria: Paging @sandeep @jen — this looks like multipathd reacting to fabric blips? Any recent fabric/firmware changes in eu-west1?

sandeep: No firmware pushes in eu-west1. We did a NIC driver bump in ap-southeast a couple days ago, not here. Pulling host dmesg now. Can you paste any kernel tails?

alex: Here's the core tail:

```
[12345.678901] nvme nvme0: controller reset (code 0x1)
[12345.679012] nvme0n1: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[12345.679123] nvme-multipath: path lost /dev/nvme0n1
[12345.680000] pci 0000:3b:00.0: link down
```

Also seeing `multipathd` restart events and a burst of `io timeout` messages.

jen: I see a correlated spike in ephemeral-cleaner starts around the same time, could GC be hammering IO and nudging timeouts?

kai: Cleaner spikes explain heavy IO, but `pci link down` reads like a fabric/PCI/driver disconnect. Are these NVMe-oF targets over RDMA or physically local NVMe? I thought these were locally attached.

alex: These hosts use NVMe-oF targets over RoCE for local-ish attach. So a fabric microburst could present as PCI link flaps at the host side.

sandeep: Network team note: there was a ~3s east-west fabric microburst at 04:12 UTC that correlates with these host errors. Opening INF-8942 to track. That could cause RoCE packet loss and controller resets.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Alert: 04:12 UTC fabric microburst detected in eu-west1 — investigating (ticket INF-8942).

jen: Short term mitigations: 1) throttle ephemeral cleaner concurrency during the instability window; 2) bump GPU attach-controller timeout to 90s and add extra retries; 3) move active attach attempts off affected racks to fallback pools.

maria: Agree on throttling cleaner. Propose a 30m rate-limit for janitor cycles in eu-west1 to reduce IO pressure while network stabilizes.

kai: Pushing a runtime canary to throttle cleaner to 10% concurrency on a few nodes: `./opsctl set janitor.concurrency=0.1 --query region=eu-west1 --canary 5` — starting canary now.

alex: :thumbsup: launching canary. Ops please avoid kernel changes for this — don't flip kernel nvme knobs mid-incident unless unavoidable.

sandeep: Agreed. Also adding a temporary scheduling rule to avoid big GPU batches on affected racks. Will coordinate with autoscaler.

network-dev: Rolling micro-configs now, expecting fabric stabilization in ~12 minutes. Will update INF-8942 when cleared.

alex: Local ops note: moved 48 pending GPU pods to fallback pool which dropped attach queue from ~75 to 3. Monitoring attach failures; keeping thread for a postmortem.

jen: PM note for postmortem: impact = ~125 GPU attach waits across fleet, 2 customer jobs delayed ~15–20m, transient cost bump from retries. Action items: janitor throttling policy, attach timeout/backoff, multipath health metric and alert.

alex: Thanks — I'll collate logs (nvme, multipathd, dmesg, network traces) and draft the postmortem after fabric clears.
